threads.thread_goal: Align on overall program scope, objectives, and roles for the pilot.

messages.text: Hello team, welcome to the official kickoff for our Integrated Creative Wellbeing Program pilot! The main objective is to design and test a multidisciplinary program for our residents over the next few weeks. The project pack has all the details.
Great to get started! I've reviewed the backlog and I'm ready to begin drafting the movement session plan for T2.

Thank you for kicking this off, @71781. The project objective is clear. To ensure we're all aligned from the start, shall we formally confirm the proposed 8-week pilot duration? That seems like a good timeframe to gather meaningful feedback.
I agree, 8 weeks is a realistic timeframe. My focus will be on ensuring the program is operationally feasible regarding room usage and staffing.
Excellent. Let's lock in the 8-week pilot then (D1). I also think it's a good idea to quickly clarify our primary responsibilities to avoid any overlap.
Ok. For my task T1, I'm designing the music session templates. Do I also need to book the rooms for those sessions?

Good question, @23126. @266482 will be handling all room mapping and booking as part of T4. Your focus for T1 will be on the therapeutic content itself, which will be a key part of our main curriculum document, A1.
Got it, thanks for clarifying.
Acknowledged. I will be responsible for the safety and emergency procedures.

Perfect. To summarize and confirm our primary responsibilities then: I'll cover spiritual/cultural components and eligibility criteria. @23126 and @97658 will design the core session content for music and dance (T1, T2). @71781, you'll manage the overall program structure and comms (T3). @266482 handles all facility logistics, and @455451 oversees safety protocols. Is everyone comfortable with this division of labor?
Works for me!
Yes, that's a clear summary.
Confirmed.
Yes, I understand now.
Excellent, we have alignment. Thanks everyone. So to recap, we've confirmed the 8-week pilot (D1) and our primary roles (D2). I'll start working on the draft schedule for T3 and share it here soon.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize weekly schedule, room allocation, and staffing feasibility.

messages.text: Hi team, as part of T3, I've created a first draft of the weekly schedule for the pilot. You can find it in the 'Room, Schedule, and Capacity Planner' (A2). I'd appreciate your feedback, especially from @266482 on room availability (T4) and @455451 on supervision needs.

Thanks @71781. I've reviewed the schedule against my room mapping from T4. The only conflict I see is the dance session in the main hall on Tuesday afternoons. That's when our floor cleaning crew does their weekly deep clean. Could we perhaps move it to the morning?
Tuesday morning works perfectly for me. Is that space generally clear of furniture? We'll need a good amount of open floor to ensure safety during the movement exercises.

The schedule looks thoughtful. I particularly appreciate the inclusion of a quiet, reflective session on Friday afternoons, which aligns well with the spiritual needs of many residents and avoids conflicts with major prayer times.

For any session involving significant movement, we must have a minimum of two staff members present for supervision. This needs to be reflected in the staffing model (T9). I will also add a 'space check' item to the pre-session checklist A5.

Great points all around. I've updated the schedule in A2 to move the dance session to Tuesday morning. @266482, can you confirm the staffing impact (T9) of the two-person supervision rule from @455451? Can we manage that?
The room for the music session seems a bit small. Will there be a place to store the smaller instruments like tambourines and shakers?

@71781, yes, we can manage the two-person rule. The model would be one therapist leading and one frontline care staff supporting. I've already spoken to the care team lead and they are on board. This staffing model seems feasible for all sessions. @23126, the music room has a large, lockable cabinet for instrument storage.

Perfect. It sounds like we can officially confirm the staffing model and supervision requirements (D4). With the final time change made, are we all happy to approve the weekly schedule and room plan in A2?
Approved from my side.
Yes, looks good.
The plan is acceptable.
Excellent, that's a consensus. D3 and D4 are confirmed. I'll mark T3 and T9 as complete. This schedule will be a key input for the staff briefing materials in T11.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on safety, emergency, and incident reporting procedures.

messages.text: As per T6, the draft 'Safety, Emergency, and Incident Protocols' (A3) is now available for review. This includes the pre-session checklist (A5) and two options for an incident report template. Please provide your feedback.

Thanks @455451. The escalation path is clear, but it lists the Clinical Coordinator as the primary contact. What's the procedure if they are not on-site during a session? We need a clearly designated backup.
I can serve as the backup contact. The on-duty accommodation manager is always reachable. I'll ensure the front desk staff are briefed. @455451, please update A3 to reflect this.

This is a very thorough draft. Regarding the incident report templates, I strongly prefer Option B. It includes fields for noting behavioral context and emotional state, which is vital for non-physical incidents. It provides a more holistic view.
What counts as an 'incident'? For example, if a resident becomes tearful during a nostalgic song, does that require a full report?

That's an important distinction to make, @23126. I would suggest that transient, self-resolving emotional responses are noted in the session log. A full incident report should be for situations that require follow-up, intervention from other staff, or pose a risk. @455451, perhaps we can add a sentence to A3 to clarify this threshold?
I agree with both points from @362587. Option B for the template, and clarifying the reporting threshold. This clarity will be essential for the staff briefing we'll be running (T11).

Agreed. I have updated A3 to include the on-duty manager as the backup contact and added a note to clarify the threshold for incident reporting. We will proceed with Option B as the final incident reporting template.
The updated protocol looks good. I'm happy to sign off on the safety checklist and the emergency escalation steps.
The backup contact makes it much more robust. I approve as well.
Looks great. Fully support.

Thank you for the feedback. We have now signed off on the safety checklist and escalation steps (D5) and selected the incident reporting template (D6). I will finalize A3 and A5 and upload them to the shared drive.

threads.thread_goal: Define resident eligibility, consent, and communication approach.

messages.text: Hello everyone. For T10, I have drafted the resident eligibility and referral criteria. The aim is to be inclusive while ensuring participant safety and wellbeing. In parallel, @71781 has prepared the draft 'Resident Information and Consent Pack' (A6) for T7. Both are ready for your review.
Thanks @362587. The info pack in A6 uses plain language and clear opt-in/opt-out instructions. I'm particularly interested in feedback on its clarity and accessibility for residents.

These look great. The criteria in the T10 doc are well-defined. For the info pack A6, would it be possible to add a simple icon or a photo next to the description of each session type? A visual cue for the dance session might make it more approachable.
In the exclusion criteria, it mentions 'severe cognitive impairment'. That seems a bit subjective. How would we measure that consistently?

An excellent point, @23126. You are right, we need a more objective measure. I will amend the criteria to state: 'Exclusion applies to residents unable to follow simple, one-step verbal instructions or safely navigate a group environment, as determined by their primary care staff during the referral process'. This provides a clearer, more functional guideline.
Love the idea of icons, @97658. I'll add them to A6 right away. I'll also update the wording to reflect the clearer criteria suggested by @362587.
The revised criteria and referral process are clear and operationally sound. No issues from my end.
The updated criteria are acceptable from a safety perspective.
Wonderful. With that clarification made, are we all in agreement to approve the resident eligibility and referral criteria?
And with the icons added, can we also approve the final resident information and consent materials in A6 for distribution?
Yes to both from me.
Yes, the new wording is much better. Approved.
Excellent. We have our decisions. I will finalize the T10 document now. This also touches on our 'Spiritual and Cultural Sensitivity Guide' (A4).

threads.thread_goal: Align on tracking, evaluation, and reporting for the pilot outcomes.

messages.text: For T8, we need to set up a way to track wellbeing. I've started a spreadsheet, A7. My idea is we can ask residents if they feel 'good', 'ok', or 'bad' before and after each session.

That's a good, simple start. To make it even more accessible, what about a visual scale with smiley faces instead of words? Also, we should think about the best time to ask – maybe during the cool-down period rather than as they're rushing out.

The visual scale is a fantastic idea. In addition to the mood check, we absolutely need to track attendance and a simple engagement metric, like 'full participation', 'partial participation', or 'observed'. This data is critical for the 'Pilot Evaluation Summary Report' (A8) that I'll be compiling for T12. I've gone ahead and added columns for these to your draft in A7, @23126.

I support this approach. It's simple, respectful, and non-intrusive. The key is to frame it as an optional check-in, not a test. Wording like 'We'd love to know how you're feeling today' maintains resident dignity and confidentiality.
From a practical standpoint, this is very feasible for the session leaders to manage. A quick visual check-in and noting attendance won't add significant workload.

The faces scale and adding attendance is much better. Thanks for adding that. So, to confirm, the data we will collect is: attendance, engagement level, and the pre/post session mood check using the visual scale?

Exactly. That's the minimal viable data set we need. Let's agree on that (D9). For the final report (A8), I propose we create a concise summary for facility management that highlights participation, key findings, and recommendations. We can have a more detailed appendix for the clinical team.
That tiered reporting strategy is wise. It ensures the right level of detail reaches the right audience. I fully support that format.
Agreed, a high-level summary is exactly what management will want to see.

Perfect. We've agreed on the data to collect (D9) and the format for the evaluation report (D10). I'll create a template for A8 based on this. @23126, can you please update the tracking log A7 with the visual scale concept and the new columns?
Yes, I will update A7 today.
